Question B-006-009-009.

Why the correct answer is right: In free space a half-wave dipole has maximum radiation broadside to the wire and nulls off the wire ends, giving a doughnut-shaped three-dimensional pattern around the antenna.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Maximum radiation from the ends of the antenna": The wire ends are where the dipole has nulls, not maxima. Confusing end-fire radiation with broadside radiation reverses the basic dipole pattern.
- sourceIndex 2: "Omnidirectional radiation pattern": A dipole is not equal in all three-dimensional directions; it has strong broadside radiation and weak radiation off the ends.
- sourceIndex 3: "Hemispherical radiation pattern": A hemisphere would put energy over one half-space. A free-space dipole pattern is a torus around the wire, with two end nulls.
